rule: Every Slither finding on the fixed tree (standard detectors and the three kestrel-* detectors, run together through the plugin) is listed here with a justification. scripts/slither-triage.mjs fails CI on any unlisted finding and on any entry that no longer matches a finding. The source carries no slither-disable comments.

entries.justification: The `from` of the transferFrom is `req.user`, whose EIP-712 signature (ECDSA or ERC-1271) over this exact request, chain and nonce was verified just before. Spending the signer's tokens is the purpose of a meta-transaction relayer.

Executing an arbitrary call with treasury ETH is the intended emergency capability. It is gated on checkpointed votes held `emergencyLookback` blocks earlier reaching 66.66% of the supply at that block, which a flash or short-term loan cannot satisfy (SC04 fix, Halmos check_flashMintCannotPassEmergencyQuorum).
Standard delegating-proxy assembly (calldatacopy, delegatecall, returndatacopy, return/revert). The frame never returns to Solidity, so scratch memory use is safe; documented in the code.
Reads the EIP-1967 admin slot. Fixed-slot storage outside the sequential layout is the SC10 fix; Solidity has no non-assembly way to address an arbitrary slot.
Writes the EIP-1967 admin slot. Fixed-slot storage outside the sequential layout is the SC10 fix; Solidity has no non-assembly way to address an arbitrary slot.
Reads the EIP-1967 implementation slot, the standard location block explorers and tooling expect; marked memory-safe.
Writes the EIP-1967 implementation slot and emits Upgraded; marked memory-safe.
Bubbles the implementation's revert data from a failed initialization delegatecall (reads only the returned bytes), the same pattern as OpenZeppelin's Address.verifyCallResult.

Batch settlement writes each tracked reserve once per listed asset; with duplicates rejected (SC05 fix) a batch over the two pool tokens performs at most two SSTOREs, so the loop cost is bounded and small.

`proposals[id].deadline == 0` is an existence check on an uninitialized storage slot (a created proposal always has deadline = block.number + votingPeriod > 0), not a balance or timestamp comparison an attacker could make unreachable.

Transparent-proxy routing: for the admin the modifier runs the function body; for anyone else it delegates to the implementation and returns or reverts from assembly, never falling through. This is the OpenZeppelin 4.x TransparentUpgradeableProxy pattern.
For non-admin callers `ifAdmin` deliberately ends the call frame with the implementation's return data (transparent proxy); the halting return is the intended behavior.

`_delegate` halts with the implementation's return data by design; the modifier relies on it to forward non-admin calls (transparent proxy).

Accepted risk, reviewed: vault-share collateral is valued at the vault's share price. That price only moves up by donation (accrue), which the first-deposit dead shares make unprofitable to manipulate (Review_VaultInflation regressions), and the price views revert while a vault operation is in flight (SC08 fix), so it cannot be read mid-redemption. The spot-priced part, the ERC-20 collateral, now uses the TWAP oracle.
Arbitrary governance execution needs a low-level call; the result is checked (ExecutionFailed) and the function is nonReentrant.
Arbitrary governance execution needs a low-level call; the result is checked (ExecutionFailed), the proposal is marked executed before the call (CEI) and the function is nonReentrant.
Native-currency refund to the caller; the result is checked and a failed refund reverts the swap (SC06 fix). It uses call, not transfer, so smart wallets with expensive receive hooks work.
Owner-only ETH withdrawal; accounting is updated before the call (CEI), the result is checked (NativeTransferFailed) and the function is nonReentrant.
Initialization delegatecall into the implementation that was just validated to be a contract; the standard proxy constructor pattern, with revert data bubbled.
Native ETH payout; the result is checked (EthTransferFailed), state is settled before the call in both withdraw and redeem (SC08 fix), and the callers are nonReentrant.

KestrelPool implements observe() with the exact signature of PoolTwapOracle's minimal IObservablePool view, which is declared next to its only consumer in src/shared. Inheriting it would make every tree's pool depend on the oracle file; the oracle's constructor call to observe() checks the interface at deployment.

A call to address(0) is a no-op (or an explicit ETH burn) that only a durable 66.66% stakeholder can trigger and could equally pass as a normal proposal; a zero check would not change the trust model.
Reward emissions accrue per second by design; a validator's few seconds of timestamp drift changes emissions by rate x seconds, which is negligible and bounded by the funded reserve.
The TWAP accumulator integrates price over elapsed seconds by construction (Uniswap v2 design); a few seconds of timestamp drift is negligible against the 30-60 minute averaging window.
Inherits the per-second reward accrual of _globalRewardUpdate; the comparison caps the payout at the funded reserve, it does not gate access.
View that brings the TWAP accumulator up to block.timestamp; the same per-second design as _syncOracle.
Signature deadline check; the user picks the deadline and a few seconds of validator drift cannot meaningfully extend an authorization.

Staleness bound on the published TWAP (reverts once the average is older than maxAge, 1 hour in the fixtures); a few seconds of validator drift cannot make a meaningfully stale price readable, and the comparison fails closed.
The event signature follows EIP-1967 exactly (AdminChanged(address previousAdmin, address newAdmin), unindexed) so standard tooling decodes it.
